evals.name: structural-happy-path
evals.prompt: Validate the COMP fixture at skills/comp/evals/fixtures/COMP-happy.md under private visibility and report whether it passes.
evals.expected_output: Runs shirabe validate --visibility private on a well-formed COMP document with all seven required sections; the document passes (exit 0) with no validation errors.
expectations: Runs validation with --visibility private (COMP is private-only)
Reports the well-formed COMP passes with no errors (exit 0)
Does not report any R9, FC01, FC02, FC03, or FC04 error

evals.name: fc04-missing-section
evals.expected_output: The fixture omits a required section, so validation under private visibility fails with an FC04 error naming the missing section.
expectations: Runs validation with --visibility private
Reports an FC04 error for the missing required section
Exit code is non-zero

evals.name: fc02-invalid-status
evals.expected_output: The fixture carries a status outside the Draft/Accepted/Done enum, so validation under private visibility fails with an FC02 error.
expectations: Runs validation with --visibility private
Reports an FC02 error for the invalid status value
Exit code is non-zero

evals.name: r9-public-rejection
evals.expected_output: COMP is private-only, so validating a well-formed COMP under public visibility fails with exactly one R9 error and no structural errors.
expectations: Runs validation with --visibility public
Reports exactly one R9 error (private-only gate)
Reports no FC01-FC04 errors
Exit code is non-zero

evals.name: r9-empty-visibility-fail-closed
evals.prompt: Validate skills/comp/evals/fixtures/COMP-happy.md with no visibility flag.
evals.expected_output: With visibility unset, the private-only gate fails closed: a well-formed COMP is still rejected with an R9 error.
expectations: Runs validation without a --visibility flag
Reports an R9 error because unset visibility fails closed (treated as not-private)
Exit code is non-zero

evals.name: r9-fires-before-fc
evals.prompt: Validate skills/comp/evals/fixtures/COMP-missing-section.md under public visibility and explain which errors fire.
evals.expected_output: Under public visibility the R9 gate short-circuits the structural checks: the only error is R9, even though the document is also missing a required section (no FC04).
expectations: Runs validation with --visibility public
Reports the R9 error
Does NOT report FC04, because R9 returns early before the structural checks run

evals.name: draft-to-accepted-transition
evals.prompt: Copy skills/comp/evals/fixtures/COMP-draft-to-accepted.md into docs/competitive/ and run shirabe transition on it to move it from Draft to Accepted.
evals.expected_output: The transition subcommand moves the COMP from Draft to Accepted, updating both frontmatter and the body Status section, with moved:false in its JSON output and no directory change.
expectations: Invokes shirabe transition <path> Accepted
Frontmatter status becomes Accepted
Body Status section first line becomes Accepted
JSON output reports moved:false (no directory movement)
Exit code is 0

evals.name: public-repo-skill-warning
evals.expected_output: Invoked in a public repo, the /comp skill detects non-private visibility at Phase 0 and warns rather than refusing: it emits '[/comp] WARNING acme-widgets: visibility=public' to stdout as a machine-readable signal, tells the author this repo is public and that COMP content is competitive and belongs in a private repo, names the consequence (shirabe validate rejects a COMP under public visibility via R9, and the CI guardrail fails the PR, so the analysis cannot be finalized here), points at the alternative of a BRIEF or PRD that references the competitive question without carrying the analysis, and asks whether to continue. The decision is presented with a recommendation rather than as a bare continue-or-stop pair: 'Stop here (Recommended)' ranks first, grounded in how visibility was resolved (the CLAUDE.md header, the inferred repo path, or an absent header), with 'Continue anyway' available. Recommending stop is not stopping -- the skill does not exit on its own; the author decides. The warning fires before any file is created or wip/ is initialized.
expectations: Plan detects repo visibility at Phase 0 from CLAUDE.md or repo path
Plan warns at Phase 0, before creating any file or initializing wip/
Plan emits the exact stdout signal '[/comp] WARNING acme-widgets: visibility=public'
Plan marks 'Stop here' as the recommended option rather than presenting continue and stop as an unranked pair
Plan grounds the recommendation by naming how visibility was resolved (CLAUDE.md header, inferred repo path, or absent header), so the author can spot a mis-set header
Plan does NOT terminate the invocation on its own; 'Continue anyway' remains available and the author decides
Plan names the alternatives (a BRIEF or PRD referencing the competitive question without the analysis)
Plan names the enforcement that still holds: validate's R9 gate and the CI guardrail reject a COMP under public visibility
Plan does NOT ask a bare 'continue or stop?' with no stated preference

evals.name: significant-fail-recommends-a-path
evals.prompt: /comp acme-widgets -- the Phase 4 jury returns a significant FAIL: the competitive-framing reviewer finds every Opportunity entry aspirational, naming no competitor that lacks the capability.
evals.expected_output: Phase 4 step 4.3 presents the significant-FAIL decision as the agent recommending a path, not as a neutral loop-back-or-reject pair. Because the failing checks are repairable by re-drafting the same competitors and dimensions, 'Loop back to Phase 3 (Recommended)' ranks first and Reject follows with a reason for ranking lower. The description names the failing check and quotes the offending Opportunity entry the reviewer flagged.
expectations: Plan marks one path '(Recommended)' rather than offering loop-back and reject unranked
Plan applies the heuristic: repairable checks favor looping back to Phase 3, a wrong competitive question favors rejecting
Plan's description names the failing rubric check and quotes the offending section or entry the reviewer flagged
Plan gives the non-recommended path a stated reason for ranking lower
Plan says so and names a tiebreaker if the two paths are genuinely balanced, rather than manufacturing a preference
Plan does NOT present loop-back and reject as equally weighted options with no recommendation
